standard_prerequisites.name: The characterisation of DM, quasi-DM, separated and quasi-separated morphisms of algebraic stacks through properties of the diagonal, and the representability of the morphisms in the factorisation of a diagonal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the start of the counted proof (source lines 949-952 and again in the other parts) as pointers to two lemmas of this chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the hypotheses into properties of the induced morphisms of algebraic spaces.

standard_prerequisites.name: The permanence and base change statements for unramified, locally quasi-finite, quasi-separated, proper and quasi-compact morphisms of algebraic spaces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked repeatedly inside the counted proof (source lines 964-989, 1021-1026, 1054-1056) as cross-chapter pointers
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the property from the composite of the comparison morphisms to the intermediate one and then to the diagonal of the morphism in question.

core_obligations: Factorise the diagonal: for all four parts the proof uses the factorisation of the diagonal of the composite through the fibre product of the source with itself over the middle stack, both maps being representable by algebraic spaces (proof lines 943-952 and the analogous openings of the other parts)

Pass to test schemes: for a scheme mapping to the middle fibre product the proof forms the two algebraic spaces of the comparison and writes down a diagram of 2-cartesian squares relating them (proof lines 953-963 and 972-983)

Transport the property inwards: the hypothesis on the composite gives the property for the outer composite of the comparison maps, and the permanence statement for algebraic spaces gives it for the inner map (proof lines 964-971, 1019-1026 and 1053-1056)

Read off the conclusion: the inner map is a base change of the morphism obtained from the test scheme, identified with the fibre product defining the diagonal of the original morphism, so the property descends to that diagonal, which is the definition of the corresponding property of the morphism (proof lines 984-993, 1027 and 1056-1057)
proof_roadmap: 把 g∘f 的对角分解为 X → X ×_Y X → X ×_Z X（两步都对代数空间可表示）。对任意概型 T → X ×_Y X 取 A = X ×_{X×_Z X} T、B = (X ×_Y X) ×_{X×_Z X} T。
由假设 A → T 具相应性质（非分歧/局部准有限/准紧且准分离/proper），用代数空间的 permanence 得 A → B 具该性质；再看 2-笛卡尔方块图，A ×_B T → T 是该性质的基变换（或与 X ×_{X×_Y X} T 等同），故 f 的对角具该性质，即 f 具相应性质。四部分同型。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects four permanence assertions: if a composite of morphisms of algebraic stacks is DM, quasi-DM, separated or quasi-separated (with the additional hypothesis that the diagonal of the second factor has the same property in the last two cases), then the first factor has that property (author lemma at source lines 928-940, label lemma-compose-after-separated). The proof (source lines 942-1058) uses the same factorisation of the diagonal of the composite in all four parts, reduces to morphisms of algebraic spaces by testing against schemes mapping to the middle fibre product, applies the permanence statement for algebraic spaces to the outer composite, checks the relevant property of the inner map by a diagram of 2-cartesian squares, and reads the conclusion off the identification of the resulting fibre product with the diagonal of the original morphism (proof lines 953-1057). The uniform diagonal computation across the four cases is the content. H3.
